texts.li: {NAME} is in {PLACE}, and every traveller on the road has passed through one sick town or another. {A_nameDef}, who sees to the colony's sick, asks the council to keep the colony apart from them until it has passed: talk across a few steps of ground, trade at arm's length, no cup shared and no hand shaken.\n\nThe travellers will notice, and some of them will mind.

[lowtech] They are burning smoke fires outside the walls of {PLACE} for {NAME}, and the people on the road carry the smell of it. {A_nameDef} has seen what a fever does in a crowded hall, and asks the council to keep the colony apart from travellers until it is over.\n\nVisitors would be met from a few steps off. Some of them will take it as an insult.

[!lowtech] The radio from {PLACE} reads out the count of the sick every evening, and it has not gone down. {A_nameDef} asks the council for a rule while {NAME} lasts: travellers kept at a distance, nobody of the colony sitting down with them.\n\nIt will cost the colony a little goodwill with every group that comes through.

li.label: Keep apart from travellers until it passes
li.outcome: Until {NAME} has passed, the colony keeps travellers at arm's length. {A_nameDef} has made sure everyone knows it.

li.label: Greet them as always
li.outcome: The colony greets travellers as it always has. {A_nameDef} thinks it a mistake, and has said so.

ColonyCouncil.DilemmaDef.label: a vigil day for the holy year

texts.li: [god] It is a holy year among {FACTION}, and the roads to {PLACE} are full of the faithful. {A_nameDef} will not walk them, with the colony's work as it is, but asks the council's leave for something nearer: one day in each week, while the year lasts, kept in vigil at {GOD}'s place, from morning until the light goes.\n\nIt is a day's work lost each week, and {A_nameDef} knows it.

[god] The pilgrims going by to {PLACE} have stirred something in {A_nameDef}, who holds to {GOD} more than anyone at the colony. {A_nameDef} asks to give {GOD} one day a week for as long as the holy year lasts, a day of vigil and no other work.\n\nThe colony would be a pair of hands short on those days.

[faith] It is a holy year among {FACTION}, and the faithful are on every road to {PLACE}. {A_nameDef} cannot go, but asks the council's leave to keep one day in each week in vigil, in the ways of {GOD}, from morning until the light goes, while the year lasts.\n\nIt is a day's work lost each week.

li.label: Grant the vigil days
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} will keep the first vigil tomorrow, and one each week after it until the holy year is done.

texts.li: {NAME} has set {FACTION} and {ENEMY} against each other, and now it has reached the council table. {A_nameDef}, who has ties among {FACTION}, wants the colony to stand with them openly: to deal with them, and give {ENEMY} nothing. {B_nameDef}, who has friends among {ENEMY}, says the colony has no business choosing, and if it chooses, it has chosen wrong.\n\nBoth of them are waiting for the council.

Supper ended early last night. {A_nameDef} spoke up for {FACTION} in {NAME}, {B_nameDef} spoke up for {ENEMY}, and by the end neither would look at the other. Now they have brought it to the council: should the colony stand with one side, and which?\n\nWhichever side it backs, the other will stop asking it for anything.

li.label: Stand with {FACTION}
li.outcome: The colony stands with {FACTION} in {NAME}, and {ENEMY} will have to look elsewhere for what they need.

li.label: Stand with {ENEMY}
li.outcome: The colony stands with {ENEMY} in {NAME}, and {FACTION} will have to look elsewhere for what they need.

li.label: Keep out of it
li.outcome: The colony keeps out of {NAME}, and deals with whoever comes to the gate, as before. {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} have agreed to leave it at that.

texts.li: {FACTION} are in mourning at {PLACE}, and {NAME} has emptied their streets of everything but black. {A_nameDef} asks that the colony show it too: dark colours worn by everyone until the mourning is over, as good neighbours do.\n\nIt costs nothing but a little dye, {A_nameDef} says, and {FACTION} will see it.

[lowtech] The bells and drums at {PLACE} have gone slow for days. {A_nameDef} says that among neighbours the dead are mourned by everyone, and asks that the colony put on dark colours for {FACTION}'s dead until {NAME} has run its course.\n\nTheir people pass the colony often enough to notice.

li.label: Wear mourning colours
li.outcome: By the council's word, the colony wears dark grey for {FACTION}'s dead until their mourning is over.

li.label: Leave the colony's clothes as they are
li.outcome: The council thinks {FACTION}'s grief is their own, and leaves it there. {A_nameDef} thinks less of the council for it.

texts.li: The fair at {PLACE} is all anyone on the road talks about: the stalls, the contests, the music going on long after dark. Nobody can be spared to walk there, so {A_nameDef} asks for the next best thing: a fair day at home, the work left where it stands and the colony out together for the day.\n\nThe day's work would wait until tomorrow.

{A_nameDef} has heard every traveller's story of the fair at {PLACE}, and is tired of hearing them. Why not a fair day of the colony's own? One day with no work, music and games outside, and everyone there.\n\nIt would cost a day's work, no more.

li.label: Hold a fair day
li.outcome: The fair day was kept: the colony's work stopped for it, and the music went on into the afternoon.

lines.li: It's not the fair at {PLACE}, but it'll do.
No work today, the council said so.
A whole day without work, I could get used to this.
Play that one again, the one from the fair.

li.label: Not this year
li.outcome: The work goes on as usual, and the fair stays something heard about on the road.
